docs.title: Welcome to DataReality Docs
docs.text:
This site hosts technical documentation and help guides for DataReality’s NUI platform: https://nui.thedatareality.org/.

Use the tabs at the top to explore Get Started, Guides, Manuals, and Reference — mirroring the structure of Docker Docs.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Sign in to NUI at https://nui.thedatareality.org/.
  2. Choose a preference in the Dashboard Overview.
  3. Explore Product Events, Event Distribution, and export data.

For step‑by‑step setup, see Get Started Overview, Installation, and What is Data Reality?.

docs.title: What’s in this documentation
docs.text:

  • Reference: glossary, data definitions, system requirements, plus APIs and UI components.

Tip: Use the search bar to find topics quickly.

docs.title: Data Pipeline
docs.text:
How data flows through DataReality from ingestion to insights:

  • Ingestion: data sources and connectors feed raw events.
  • Processing: normalization, enrichment, and validation.
  • Storage: partitioned tables for events and reference data.
  • Analytics: dashboards and trend tracking built on aggregated views.
  • Export: raw and filtered datasets available for download.

Related guides: Downloading Raw Data, Tracking Event Trends, Dashboard Overview.

docs.title: Deployment Topology
docs.text:
Recommended deployment layout and network boundaries:

  • Reverse proxy with TLS at the edge, routing UI and API.
  • Application services in a private network segment.
  • Database and analytics stores protected by security groups.
  • Static site hosting for documentation under /docs/.
  • CI/CD: build, test, and deploy pipelines for app and docs.

Refer to: System Requirements and Security & Compliance.

docs.title: Platform Architecture Overview
docs.text:
This section provides a high-level view of the DataReality platform architecture, including the client (NUI), backend services, data storage, and external systems.

  • Core components: NUI frontend, API layer, data processing workers, storage (OLTP + analytics), and integrations.
  • Deployment: containerized services behind a reverse proxy; static docs are served separately.
  • Observability: logging, metrics, and tracing across services.
  • Security: role-based access, authentication, and data protection.

See also: System Requirements, REST API, and Security & Compliance.

docs.title: Security Model
docs.text:
Security principles and access control used by DataReality:

  • Authentication: SSO or local accounts via the API.
  • Authorization: roles and permissions guard features and data.
  • Data protection: encryption in transit (TLS) and at rest.
  • Audit: activity logging for sensitive operations.
  • Compliance: mapping to applicable standards.

See also: Manuals → Security and compliance; Roles and permissions.

docs.title: Get DataReality
docs.text: DataReality is a platform for post‑market surveillance, quality event monitoring, and regulatory workflows. It centralizes device event data, recall information, and reporting so you can analyze trends, mitigate risk, and stay audit‑ready.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Note - You need a company account to access NUI. - Ask your administrator for a role (Viewer, Analyst, Admin). - See the System Requirements for supported browsers and access prerequisites.

docs.title: Accessing DataReality
docs.text:
• Sign in at https://nui.thedatareality.org/.
  • Confirm your region and time window in the dashboard header.
  • Use search to find preferences (products) and pin favorites.

docs.title: Choose your path
docs.text:

  • Installation — set up internal access and environment.

docs.title: Dashboard Overview
docs.text: The dashboard is the first screen after login and summarizes activity for the selected product preference.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
• Events: count of all reported events in the selected window.
  • Serious Injuries: events marked with serious patient outcomes.
  • Malfunctions: device malfunction incidents linked to the preference.

docs.title: Filtering controls
docs.text:
• By Report Date: filters by the date a record was reported to the authority.
  • By Event Date: filters by when the event actually occurred.
  • Time window presets: 1 Year, 6 Months, or a custom range.
  • Region: choose US or EU to scope metrics.

Use the header controls to switch between date anchors, adjust timeframes, and focus on regional trends.

docs.title: Understanding Event Distribution
docs.text:
The donut chart shows the distribution of event categories for the selected preference and window.

  • Percentage vs Number: toggle to view either relative share or absolute counts.
  • Largest percentage: highlights the dominant category (e.g., Active Events) — use this to identify focus areas.
  • Hover tooltips: reveal labels, counts, and percentages for each segment.

docs.title: Navigation Menu
docs.text:
The left menu organizes core functions:

  • Risk Analysis: hazard identification, scoring (Likelihood × Severity), mitigation tracking.
  • Compliance: regulatory tests, CRA, Audit, Vigilance reporting, PSUR generation.
  • Reporting: exports, dashboards, saved views, and distribution visuals.

Each section contains subpages documented in the Guides and Manuals.

docs.title: Selecting Your Product
docs.text: Use the selector bar to switch between preferences such as Starclose, Prostar, VIP, PerClose, Mynx, and SStplus.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
• Use the "Search preferences…" bar to quickly locate a product by name.
  • Click the arrow controls to move to adjacent preferences without typing.
  • Favorites: pin high‑priority preferences for one‑click access.

docs.title: What is Data Reality?
docs.text:
Data Reality is a Post‑Market Surveillance and Quality Event Monitoring platform.

It centralizes device event data, recall information, and regulatory workflows to help organizations maintain compliance and reduce risk.

docs.title: Primary goals
docs.text:
• Compliance and audit readiness: align with regulatory reporting requirements and maintain an auditable history.
  • Risk mitigation: identify trends early and prioritize corrective actions.
  • Operational insights: support Engineering, Quality, Safety, and Regulatory teams with actionable dashboards and exports.

docs.title: Who uses Data Reality?
docs.text:
• Quality and Safety teams monitoring events and injuries
  • Regulatory teams preparing Vigilance, PSUR, or CRA documentation
  • Product teams tracking malfunctions and corrective actions

docs.title: Analyzing Event Details
docs.text: Drill down by clicking metrics such as "54 Events" or "3 Serious Injuries" to open the detailed list.

docs.title: Detail view attributes
docs.text:
• Event ID
  • Date Reported
  • Event Date
  • Severity
  • Product Lot
  • Region (US/EU)

Use filters to refine the list and open individual event records. From the record, export or link to associated recalls and mitigation actions.

docs.title: Dashboard Overview
docs.text:
The Dashboard provides a high‑level summary of events, recalls, and distribution.

  • Header controls: report date vs event date, time range, and region.
  • Cards: Total Events, Serious Injuries, Malfunctions, Recalls.
  • Views: Graph view, Table view, and period granularity.

Use this section to monitor trends and identify outliers.

docs.title: Data Export
docs.text:
Export raw data for offline analysis.

  • Choose Download Raw Data from the dashboard.
  • Select format (CSV/JSON) and time window.
  • Ensure role permissions allow data export.

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
1. Click "Download Raw Data" in the dashboard header.
  2. Choose format (CSV or Excel) and select the time range.
  3. Confirm filters (date anchor and region) before downloading.

docs.title: Included fields
docs.text:
• Event ID, Report Date, Event Date, Severity, Category
  • Product name, lot, model
  • Region, source, and recall linkage

docs.title: Events and Recalls
docs.text:
This page explains how events and recalls are collected, normalized, and presented.

  • Event sources: internal databases and regulatory feeds.
  • Recall detection: automated matching and periodic audits.
  • Interpretation: Severity, frequency, and contextual metadata.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: This section describes how internal users set up access and configure the environment.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Company account on DataReality NUI.
  • Appropriate role assigned (viewer, analyst, admin).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Request access from your administrator.
  2. Log in to https://nui.thedatareality.org/.
  3. Confirm region and time window in the dashboard header.
  4. Bookmark frequently used preferences for quick navigation.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: • Continue with the Quick demo.

docs.title: Preferences Monitoring
docs.text:
Preferences represent devices or categories under observation.

  • Search and select a preference using the search bar.
  • Use the arrow navigation to browse adjacent preferences.
  • Save favorites for quick access.

docs.title: Quick Demo
docs.text:
Follow this mini tour to understand the core workflow:

  1. Open Dashboard Overview and select a preference.
  2. Review Total Events and Recalls metrics.
  3. Switch the period granularity between Month, Week, and Day.
  4. Open Event Distribution and hover over segments to see counts.
  5. Use search to filter preferences and export raw data.

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
1. Open the Regulatory Test module from the left menu.
  2. Choose the test type (e.g., product batch, device type) and scope.
  3. Configure inputs and initiate the run.
  4. Monitor progress until completion.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
• Pass/Fail status with summary metrics.
  • Detailed report with failures, affected lots, and remediation notes.
  • Export as PDF/CSV for audit or compliance submissions.

docs.title: Tracking Event Trends
docs.text: Use Table view to inspect monthly breakdowns (e.g., Dec 2024, Jan 2025).

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
• Event: total events for the period.
  • Death: reported deaths.
  • Malfunction: device malfunction counts.
  • Injury: injuries associated with the preference.

docs.title: How to read the table
docs.text:
• Sort by any column to surface trends.
  • Click a cell to drill into the underlying event list for that period.
  • Switch between Month, Week, and Day to adjust granularity.

docs.text:

docs.title: Integrations Overview
docs.text:
Supported integration surfaces:

  • REST API for programmatic access and automation.
  • Webhooks for event-driven notifications.
  • Data exports for batch ingestion into external systems.
  • Authentication/SSO options for user management.

See: Reference → REST API; Guides → Data Export.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text:
Receive notifications when specific events occur:

  • Subscription model and event types.
  • Delivery format and retries.
  • Security (signing, IP allowlists).
  • Handling failures and replay strategies.

Links: Operational Workflows; Incident Response.

docs.title: CRA (Compliance Risk Assessment)
docs.text:
• Assess risk against applicable regulations (e.g., EU MDR, FDA guidance).
  • Map controls and evidence to regulatory clauses.
  • Generate risk ratings and recommended actions.

docs.title: Audit Log
docs.text:
• Search by user, action, date, or entity.
  • Filter and export the complete audit trail for external review.
  • Maintain immutable records supporting inspections.

docs.title: RPN
docs.text:
• Risk Priority Number = Severity × Occurrence × Detection.
  • Use RPN thresholds to prioritize actions and reviews.

docs.title: FMEA Structure
docs.text:
• Failure Mode: what can go wrong.
  • Effects: outcomes to patient/product.
  • Causes: root causes and contributing factors.
  • Controls: current controls and recommended mitigations.

docs.title: Risk Scoring
docs.text:
• Methodology: Likelihood × Severity to compute relative risk.
  • Calibration: define scales for likelihood and severity consistent with your QMS.

docs.title: Mitigation Tracking
docs.text:
• Create corrective actions tied to hazards.
  • Track owner, status, due dates, and verification of effectiveness.
  • Link mitigations to events or failure modes for traceability.

docs.title: Roles and Permissions
docs.text:
Access levels and permissions across the NUI platform.

  • Viewer: Read‑only access to dashboards and exports.
  • Analyst: Can create saved views and run deeper analyses.
  • Admin: Manages users, roles, and platform configuration.

docs.title: Security and Compliance
docs.text:
Overview of security posture and compliance requirements.

  • Data retention policies and audit trails.
  • Regulatory alignment for healthcare and device monitoring.
  • Incident response and contact channels.

docs.title: Terminology
docs.text:
Key terms used throughout the platform and documentation.

  • Preference: A device or category under monitoring.
  • Event: A recorded incident or observation.
  • Recall: A manufacturer or regulatory action related to a preference.

docs.title: Reporting Workflow
docs.text:
1. Select report type: Vigilance or PSUR.
  2. Confirm scope, time window, and affected products.
  3. Populate required fields and attach supporting evidence.
  4. Review, validate, and export the report.

docs.title: Required Fields
docs.text:
• Reporting Authority
  • Patient Outcome
  • Event summaries, severity distributions
  • Product and lot details

docs.title: Product Modules Overview
docs.text:
This section introduces the core modules in DataReality and links to detailed guides.

  • Dashboard: visualize trends and KPIs.
  • Events & Recalls: track and analyze event records.
  • Regulatory Test: run compliance-focused checks.
  • Data Export: extract datasets for external analytics.
  • Preferences: customize monitoring and alerts.

See detailed Guides for each module.

docs.title: Data Definitions
docs.text:
Field‑by‑field descriptions used across the platform.

  • Severity Score: numeric rating representing outcome seriousness (defined by QMS).
  • Event ID: unique identifier for a recorded event.
  • Date Reported vs Event Date: reporting date vs occurrence date.
  • Region: market region associated with the record (US/EU).
  • Product Lot: batch/lot identification tying events to manufacturing.

docs.title: Glossary of Terms
docs.text:
• FMEA: Failure Mode and Effects Analysis.
  • CRA: Compliance Risk Assessment.
  • 510(k): US FDA premarket notification route.
  • PSUR: Periodic Safety Update Report.
  • Event: recorded incident associated with a device or product.
  • Malfunction: device issue causing failure of intended operation.
  • Injury: patient injury linked to an event; can be serious or non‑serious.
  • Recalls: regulatory/manufacturer actions affecting products.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
• Supported browsers: Chrome, Firefox (latest two versions).
  • Permissions matrix: Analyst, Administrator, Viewer roles with respective access.
  • Network: allow HTTPS access to nui.thedatareality.org and API endpoints.

docs.title: Incident Response
docs.text:
Process for handling critical issues:

  • Detection: alerts from dashboards or external monitors.
  • Assessment: severity, impact, and affected products.
  • Action: mitigation steps and stakeholder communication.
  • Post-incident: root-cause analysis and follow-up tasks.

Reference: Vigilance & PSUR Reporting; CRA & Audit.

docs.title: Operational Workflows
docs.text:
Key workflows for daily operations:

  • Event triage: identify, tag, and prioritize incoming events.
  • Investigation: analyze details, distribution, and history.
  • Escalation: create tasks and notify stakeholders.
  • Reporting: build dashboards and export datasets.

Links: Analyzing Event Details, Events & Recalls, Dashboard.

docs.title: Release Process
docs.text:
How changes move from development to production:

  • Planning: scope, dependencies, and risk assessment.
  • Build & test: automated checks and review gates.
  • Deployment: staged rollout and validation.
  • Communication: release notes and support updates.

See: Resources → Release notes; System Requirements.
